taxonomy.nativeClimate: Warm, dry summers and mild winters

care.watering: Low: Let the soil dry out entirely between waterings. Highly susceptible to overwatering.
care.soil: Sandy, gravelly, well-draining soil. It thrives in poor, rocky conditions.
care.pruning: Prune back by about one-third after flowering to keep it compact. Never cut into old, dead wood.
care.toxicityNote: Lavender contains small amounts of linalool, which are mildly toxic to dogs and cats.
care.bestFor: Gardeners with sunny, dry yards looking for a low-maintenance, fragrant perennial.

vastu.notes: In modern Vastu, lavender is famous for its calming properties.

lighting.description: Requires intense, direct sunlight to produce its signature oils and flowers.

nutrients.micronutrientNotes: Lavender actually prefers poor soil. Too much fertilizer leads to floppy, weak growth and fewer flowers.
nutrients.fertilizerFrequency: Do not fertilize. A light top-dressing of compost in the spring is more than enough.
nutrients.organicOptions: A handful of crushed eggshells can help boost the soil's alkalinity.

relationships.notes: Lavender's worst enemy is wet feet.

faq.question: Is lavender toxic to dogs or cats?
faq.answer: Lavender contains small amounts of linalool, which is mildly toxic to dogs, cats, and horses if eaten in large quantities.

faq.question: How often should I water my outdoor lavender?
faq.answer: Once established, almost never. Lavender is incredibly drought-tolerant. Only water during extended dry spells.

shortDesc: A hardy, aromatic perennial herb prized for its purple flowers and soothing fragrance.
content:
Overview

If there's one herb that truly transforms a garden, it's lavender.
quickAnswer: Lavender needs three things to thrive: full blazing sun, gritty fast-draining soil, and very little water.

troubleshooting.symptom: Plant is turning brown, yellow, and mushy from the bottom up
troubleshooting.diagnosis: Root rot due to overwatering or heavy clay soil
troubleshooting.treatment: Stop watering immediately. If in a pot, repot into dry, sandy soil.

troubleshooting.symptom: Plant is splitting open in the middle and looks woody
troubleshooting.treatment: Start pruning the green tips regularly to encourage bushiness, but do not cut into the dead wood.

glossaryTerms.definition: The thick, hard, brown stems that develop at the base of aging herbs.

summary: Lavandula angustifolia is an aromatic perennial herb that thrives in full sun, lean alkaline soils, and dry root conditions.
keyTakeaways: Plant in gritty, lean, well-draining alkaline soil within porous terracotta containers.
Provide at least 6 to 8 hours of direct, unfiltered sunlight daily.

plantHero.water: Let the soil dry out entirely between waterings.

sections.content: Water Lavender only when the top several inches of soil are dry to the touch.
